title: Consolidate overlapping skill families (router + references/)
description: Always-on skill cost is ~5,900 tokens/conversation (measured: rendered <available_skills> block = 23,246 chars, 70 skills). Consolidation is the dominant fix: ~2,200 net token savings. Merge into routers with references/: session x6->1 (close, park, next, renew, resume-handoff, create-handoff), review x7->1 (code-review, rule-of-5, rule-of-5-universal, parallel-review, multi-agent-review, guided-review, red-team-review), planning x6->2, *-diagnostician x12->1 (shared skeleton, distinct content — router desc must enumerate domains), docs x4->2, prompt-meta x3->1. Note: diagnostician bodies are NOT identical (different personas/GUARDs/taxonomies/step counts) — split content into references/, keep router SKILL.md thin. Blast radius: manifest.json entries+bundles, scripts/generate-pi-resources.mjs, install.sh, CHANGELOG, /skill:name names, version-pinned installed copies in other repos (npm:0.9.0). Ship old names as thin pointer skills for one release, then remove.

title: close skill: hardcoded journal default (~/dev/status + log/) wrong for non-interactive agent shells
description: content/distilled/close/SKILL.md lines 11+17 default JOURNAL_PATH to ~/dev/status and JOURNAL_LOG_SUBDIR to log/. .bashrc:37-39 exports the real values (JORNAL=~/para/areas/jornal, subdir areas/log) but non-interactive agent shells never source .bashrc, so every agent /close run falls back to the stale ~/dev/status clone and the wrong log/ layout. Evidence: repo history had 09-03/04/05 session notes in log/ (migrated to areas/log/ in journal commit e4f144e). Fix options: (a) flip the skill default to $HOME/para/areas/jornal + areas/log, or (b) have the skill source ~/.bashrc / read JORNAL explicitly when JOURNAL_PATH is unset. Ship with next npm release; also export JOURNAL_PATH in the agent shell config if one exists.
close_reason: Shipped in 0868ae0 + 53cfbd0: sourcing-subshell resolver, acceptance-tested verbatim in env -i

title: Trim over-long skill descriptions selectively (>150 chars)
description: Descriptions total 7,931 chars (~1,982 tok) across 70 skills and are the largest trimmable always-on component. Measured ceiling: capping ALL descs at 100 chars saves only 584 tok (7,931 -> 5,593 chars) — most descs are already short. CONSTRAINT: description is the model's only trigger signal. Blind <=100-char capping risks wrong-skill activation for near-duplicate pairs (anti-slop 230ch vs anti-slop-prose 159ch rely on descriptive detail to disambiguate). Do: trim only descriptions >150 chars; preserve distinguishing phrases; keep disambiguation pairs deliberately differentiated. Expected saving: ~400-580 tok.

title: Hide command-like skills via disable-model-invocation
description: pi excludes skills with 'disable-model-invocation: true' from the system prompt (verified in dist/core/skills.js:262,276 — still invocable via /skill:name). Apply ONLY to command-like skills the user invokes deliberately: next, park, whisper (~420 tok for 5 candidates incl. close/renew). Do NOT hide close/renew: they are plausibly prose-triggered ('wrap up the session') and hiding removes natural-language activation. Expected saving: ~250-420 tok.

title: Add source/distilled version-consistency check to sync-manifest
description: Rule-of-5 review of the file-headers implementation found version drift between source frontmatter and distilled version markers on 3 of 4 touched skills (tdd, create-issues reconciled; code-review perpetuated). Automated guard: in `just sync-manifest` (or validate-distilled), compare the `<!-- skill: NAME, version: X -->` marker in the distilled file against the source frontmatter `version:` field for each manifest entry and fail on mismatch. Evidence: prompt-task-iterative-code-review.md was 1.2.0 while distilled/code-review/SKILL.md was 1.3.0.

title: Release incitaciones (npm patch) + reinstall skills to ship cartography v1.4.0 content
description: Commits 03f2492 + 7f080af changed codebase-cartography distilled content (weight bar, Composition block, decision record; prompt-task v1.4.0). Not in any published npm version. Steps: npm version patch → git push --tags (CI .github/workflows/npm-publish.yml publishes) → reinstall locally: pi install npm:incitaciones and npx incitaciones install → verify installed ~/.agents/skills + ~/.config/agents/skills copies match the new content.

description:
Content of v0.7.0+ on npm is behind main: reworked codebase-cartography HTML export (docs/cartography/ dir, index, nav, vendored Mermaid v9.4.3) and corrected install docs (README, CLAUDE.md, site landing page) are only installed locally via repo CLI.

title: Sync issue-tracker-review source prompt with verifiable-value-claim checks
description:
**Context:** The distilled issue-review skill gained Pass 0 staleness checks (PRE-003/PRE-004 base_commit freshness) and Pass 5 verifiability checks (Meter/Must/anti-goals) based on research-paper-agentic-ticket-requirements-engineering.md. The 804-line source prompt content/prompt-task-issue-tracker-review.md does not reflect these.
Ref: content/research-paper-agentic-ticket-requirements-engineering.md

**Files / Systems:**
- content/prompt-task-issue-tracker-review.md

**Verifiable Value Claim:**

**Meter:** grep -cE 'PRE-003|PRE-004|Meter' content/prompt-task-issue-tracker-review.md (>= 4)

title: Fix lefthook check-links false positives (59 broken-link reports in research-*.md)
description: Pre-commit hook 'links' recipe reports 59 broken links in research-agentic-alignment.md, research-prompt-frameworks.md, research-value-delivery-verification.md. The reported 'targets' are bold list-item text (e.g. '**CrewAI**: Agents produce...') — the checker appears to misparse list items as markdown links. All failures predate commit c1cbe66; new files from this session are clean. Investigate the link parser in justfile recipe 'check-links' and either fix the parsing or whitelist bold-list syntax.

title: pi install update does not re-sync skills on version bump
description:
When pi install or pi update --force installs a new version of an npm package (e.g., incitaciones from 0.3.0 to 0.3.1), it refreshes the npm package in .pi/agent/npm/node_modules/ but does NOT re-copy the skills from pi-package/skills/ to the skills directories. This leaves stale installed skills at the old version.

The skills only get copied on the first pi install. Subsequent pi update reports success but leaves the skills directory untouched.

Steps to reproduce:
1. Install incitaciones@0.3.0: pi install npm:incitaciones
2. Bump to 0.3.1, publish, regenerate pi-package
3. Remove stale skills from ~/.agents/skills/
4. Run: pi update npm:incitaciones --force
5. Observe: skills directory is NOT repopulated, npm package is updated

Expected: pi update should re-copy skills from the packages pi-package/skills/ to the skills directory on version change.

Two active skill directories were observed: ~/.agents/skills and ~/.config/agents/skills with different inodes but identical content
acceptance_criteria:
1. Pi update --force re-copies skills from pi-package/skills/ to the configured skills directories
2. Installed-version stamp in SKILL.md frontmatter reflects the new version
3. Removing the skills directory and running pi update restores it
4. Regression: skills from unrelated packages are not altered
close_reason: Fixed in 0.3.2. generate-pi-resources.mjs now includes reSyncFlatInstallSkills() that detects and re-syncs flat-install skill dirs on postinstall. Tested: removing skills from ~/.agents/skills/ + running the generator restores them with npm:0.3.2 stamp.

title: Re-measure always-on skill token cost after fixes (acceptance criterion)
description: Acceptance gate for the token-reduction work: rerun the measurement (render <available_skills> block per pi dist/core/skills.js format: name+description+absolute location in XML tags; count chars/4). Baseline: 23,246 chars ~= 5,900 tok for 70 skills. Target: ~2,700-3,000 tok (~50% reduction). Also re-verify trigger behavior after consolidation: consolidated router descriptions must still activate correctly for representative phrasings of each merged family.

title: Move oversized skill bodies into references/ (doc-link-verifier, multi-agent-review)
description: On-demand cost is the lesser problem (bodies load only on trigger) but two bodies are outliers: doc-link-verifier (210 lines, ~15k chars ~= 3.7k tok per load) and multi-agent-review (196 lines, ~7.2k chars). Move detailed templates/criteria into references/ per the multi-file progressive-disclosure pattern already used by 30 skills in this repo. Low priority — only worth doing alongside consolidation.
